title: "Bayesian Estimation"
format: html
---

Change the parameters below and re-run the notebook.

```{r}
p <- 0.3                     # probability of outcome 1: 0 to 1
n <- 20                      # number of trials: 1 to 100
```

```{r}
makedata <- function() {
  set.seed(1)
  rbinom(n, 1, p)            # n Bernoulli(p) samples
}

data <- makedata()
data
```

```{r}
plot(1:n, data, pch = 19, xlab = "Trial", ylab = "Outcome")
```

# Maximum Likelihood

Compute the maximum log-likelihood for the estimate $\theta$ of $p$ for data $y_i \in \{0,1\}$.

$$
\ell(\theta) := \sum_{i=1}^n \left( y_i \cdot \log \theta + (1-y_i) \log(1-\theta) \right)
$$

```{r}
ell <- function(theta) sum(data * log(theta) + (1 - data) * log(1 - theta))
```

**Maximum likelihood:** Compute $\theta^\star \in \arg\max_{\theta \in [0,1]} \ell(\theta)$

```{r}
theta_opt <- sum(data) / n
theta_opt
```

```{r}
theta <- seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 300)
plot(theta, sapply(theta, ell), type = "l",
     xlab = expression("Parameter" ~ theta), ylab = expression("log-likelihood" ~ ell))
points(theta_opt, ell(theta_opt), pch = 19, col = "blue")
```

# Posterior Distribution

Suppose that $\Theta$ is the random variable that represents the distribution of the estimate $\theta$. We use $Y = (Y_1, \ldots, Y_n)$ to represent the random dataset with a specific value denoted as $y = (y_1, \ldots, y_n)$.

**Prior**. Assume that
$$
\Theta \sim \operatorname{Beta}(\alpha, \beta)
$$
Where [Beta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta_distribution) is the [conjugate prior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjugate_prior) for Bernoulli. See the wikipedia page for more examples of priors that work with other random variables.

**Posterior**: use Bayes theorem

$$
\mathbb{P}[\Theta = \theta \mid Y = y]
= \frac{\mathbb{P}[Y = y \mid \Theta = \theta ] \cdot \mathbb{P}[\Theta = \theta]}{\mathbb{P}[Y = y]}
$$

For the conjugate prior distribution:
$$
\Theta \mid Y = y \quad \sim \quad
\operatorname{Beta}\left(\alpha + \sum_{i=1}^n y_i, \beta + \sum_{i=1}^n (1-y_i) \right)
$$

For more advanced use, see [Bayesian linear regression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayesian_linear_regression) and [Stan](https://mc-stan.org/).

```{r}
alpha <- 1                   # prior parameter: 1 to 10
beta <- 1                    # prior parameter: 1 to 10
```

```{r}
theta <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 300)
plot(theta, dbeta(theta, alpha, beta), type = "l", xlab = expression(theta), ylab = "")
```

```{r}
plot(theta, dbeta(theta, alpha + sum(data), beta + (n - sum(data))), type = "l",
     xlab = expression(theta), ylab = "")
```
